claim: The yeast Chd1 protein acts to position nucleosomes across genomes.
source: The yeast Chd1 protein acts to position nucleosomes across genomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract summarizing the function of Chd1.

claim: In the apo state, the DNA-binding domain contacts the edge of the nucleosome.
source: In the apo state, the DNA-binding domain contacts the edge of the nucleosome while in the presence of the non-hydrolyzable ATP analog, ADP-beryllium fluoride, we observe additional interactions between the ATPase domain and the adjacent DNA gyre 1.5 helical turns from the dyad axis of symmetry.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the presence of ADP-beryllium fluoride, there are additional interactions between the ATPase domain and the adjacent DNA gyre 1.5 helical turns from the dyad axis of symmetry.
source: In the apo state, the DNA-binding domain contacts the edge of the nucleosome while in the presence of the non-hydrolyzable ATP analog, ADP-beryllium fluoride, we observe additional interactions between the ATPase domain and the adjacent DNA gyre 1.5 helical turns from the dyad axis of symmetry.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM data.

claim: Binding in the engaged conformation involves unravelling the outer turn of nucleosomal DNA.
source: Binding in this conformation involves unravelling the outer turn of nucleosomal DNA and requires substantial reorientation of the DNA-binding domain with respect to the ATPase domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM and FRET data.

claim: Binding in the engaged conformation requires substantial reorientation of the DNA-binding domain with respect to the ATPase domains.
source: Binding in this conformation involves unravelling the outer turn of nucleosomal DNA and requires substantial reorientation of the DNA-binding domain with respect to the ATPase domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparisons.

claim: The orientation of the DNA-binding domain is mediated by sequences in the N-terminus.
source: The orientation of the DNA-binding domain is mediated by sequences in the N-terminus and mutations to this part of the protein have positive and negative effects on Chd1 activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by mutagenesis and biochemical data.

claim: Mutations to the N-terminus have positive and negative effects on Chd1 activity.
source: The orientation of the DNA-binding domain is mediated by sequences in the N-terminus and mutations to this part of the protein have positive and negative effects on Chd1 activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by activity assays.

claim: The unfavorable alignment of C-terminal DNA-binding region in solution contributes to an auto-inhibited state.
source: These observations indicate that the unfavorable alignment of C-terminal DNA-binding region in solution contributes to an auto-inhibited state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nucleosomes are aligned with respect to regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes.
source: Nucleosomes are not distributed randomly over the genomes of eukaryotes, but in general are aligned with respect to regulatory elements.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited in the introduction.

claim: The spacing between nucleosomes is not random, with distinct nucleosome-to-nucleosome distances evident in different tissues and species.
source: In addition, the spacing between nucleosomes is also not random, with distinct nucleosome-to-nucleosome distances evident in different tissues and in different species (Hughes et al., 2012; van Holde, 1988).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Abnormal inter-nucleosome spacing has been associated with increased intragenic transcription.
source: Abnormal inter-nucleosome spacing has been associated with increased intragenic transcription, and changes to nucleosome positioning at promoters results in changes to gene expression (Raveh-Sadka et al., 2012; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Changes to nucleosome positioning at promoters results in changes to gene expression.
source: Abnormal inter-nucleosome spacing has been associated with increased intragenic transcription, and changes to nucleosome positioning at promoters results in changes to gene expression (Raveh-Sadka et al., 2012; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Isw1 and Chd1 enzymes both play a major role in positioning nucleosomes over coding regions.
source: For example, the Isw1 and Chd1 enzymes both play a major role in positioning nucleosomes over coding regions (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Ocampo et al., 2016; Radman-Livaja et al., 2012; Yen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Chd1 and Isw1 enzymes belong to an extended family of Snf2-related chromatin proteins.
source: These enzymes belong to an extended family of Snf2-related chromatin proteins that can act to reconfigure DNA-protein interactions (Flaus et al., 2006), with many acting on nucleosomes.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Snf2-related chromatin proteins share an ATPase module comprised of two RecA-related domains capable of ATP-dependent DNA translocation.
source: This family of proteins share an ATPase module comprised of two RecA-related domains capable of ATP-dependent DNA translocation (Havas et al., 2000; Lia et al., 2006; Saha et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The crystal structure of the ATPase domain in association with the N-terminal tandem chromodomains of Chd1 has been determined by crystallography.
source: The crystal structure of the ATPase domain in association with the N-terminal tandem chromodomains has been determined by crystallography (Hauk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: In the crystal structure of Chd1 chromoATPase domains, the chromodomains impede access to a putative DNA-binding surface between the RecA domains.
source: In this structure, the chromodomains impede access to a putative DNA-binding surface between the RecA domains, suggesting that reconfiguration is required in order for the RecA domains to engage productively with DNA.
evidence: This is an observation from a cited crystal structure.

claim: Mutation of the chromodomains at the chromo-RecA interface increased the ATPase activity of Chd1.
source: Supporting this, mutation of the chromodomains at the chromo-RecA interface increased the ATPase activity of Chd1 (Hauk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Mutations in a region N-terminal to the ATPase domains of the Drosophila ISWI protein increase ATP-hydrolysis and remodelling activity.
source: Mutations in a region N-terminal to the ATPase domains of the Drosophila ISWI protein increase ATP-hydrolysis and remodelling activity (Clapier and Cairns, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The conformation of the N-terminal region of ISWI changes during ISWI action.
source: Interestingly, the conformation of this region changes during ISWI action (Mueller-Planitz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The Chd1 protein has a C-terminal DNA-binding domain (DBD) that is made up of SANT and SLIDE domains.
source: The Chd1 protein has a C-terminal DNA-binding domain (DBD) that is made up of SANT and SLIDE domains that are also present in ISWI proteins (Grüne et al., 2003; Ryan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The C-terminal DNA-binding domain is required for efficient nucleosome repositioning in Chd1.
source: This second DNA-binding interface is required for efficient nucleosome repositioning both in the context of Chd1 (Patel et al., 2013; Ryan et al., 2011; Sharma et al., 2011) and ISWI proteins (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Grüne et al., 2003; Hota et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Substitution of the Chd1 DBD with a heterologous DBD directs nucleosome positioning towards the DNA bound by this domain.
source: Remarkably, substitution of this domain with a heterologous DBD directs nucleosome positioning towards the DNA bound by this domain (McKnight et al., 2011; Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The ATPase domain of ISW2 engages with nucleosomal DNA near super helical location (SHL) 2, two turns from the dyad axis of symmetry.
source: Application of this approach to study the ISW2 enzyme showed that the ATPase domain engages with nucleosomal DNA near super helical location (SHL) 2, two turns from the dyad axis of symmetry.
evidence: This is established knowledge from directed crosslinking studies.

claim: In ISW2, the DNA-binding accessory subunits engage linker DNA extending up to 50 bp from the edge of the nucleosome.
source: In the case of ISW2, the DNA-binding accessory subunits are observed to engage linker DNA extending up to 50 bp from the edge of the nucleosome (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Kagalwala et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Two ISWI complexes can engage a single nucleosome.
source: In the case of ISWI containing enzymes, it has been shown that two complexes can engage a single nucleosome (Racki et al., 2009) and this can facilitate the bidirectional movement of nucleosomes (Blosser et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: DNA is removed from nucleosomes in kinetically coupled bursts of 3 bp that comprise of shorter single base increments during repositioning.
source: These studies show that DNA is removed from nucleosomes in kinetically coupled bursts of 3 bp that comprise of shorter single base increments (Deindl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: A series of fragments of Chd1 were expressed and purified for SAXS analysis.
source: To help characterise the structure of intact Chd1, a series of fragments of Chd1 were expressed and purified (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: SAXS data were collected for each Chd1 fragment.
source: We then collected small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) data for each of these (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The hydrodynamic radius and molecular weight values obtained from SAXS are consistent with Chd1 being predominantly monomeric in solution.
source: For each fragment, the hydrodynamic radius of the protein fragment and molecular weight in solution was calculated (Figure 1B). The values obtained are consistent with Chd1 being predominantly monomeric in solution.
evidence: This is an interpretation of SAXS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Volumes consistent with each scattering curve were calculated ab initio for Chd1 fragments.
source: Volumes consistent with each scattering curve were calculated ab initio (Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the computational analysis of SAXS data.

claim: The DBD can be docked within the volume obtained for the DBD fragment of Chd1.
source: For example, the DBD can be docked within the volume obtained for this fragment of the protein and the chromoATPase domains within the volumes obtained for fragments that include this region.
evidence: This describes the fitting of known structures into SAXS volumes.

claim: The chromoATPase domains can be docked within the volumes obtained for fragments that include this region.
source: For example, the DBD can be docked within the volume obtained for this fragment of the protein and the chromoATPase domains within the volumes obtained for fragments that include this region.
evidence: This describes the fitting of known structures into SAXS volumes.

claim: The DBD and N-terminal 133 residues contribute to the protrusion adjacent to one of the ATPase domains in the SAXS volume.
source: This indicates that the DBD and N-terminal 133 residues contribute to the protrusion adjacent to one of the ATPase domains (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an interpretation of SAXS data.

claim: A cys-free mutant of Chd1 displays nucleosome remodelling activity comparable to the wild-type protein.
source: Importantly, this cys-free mutant protein displays nucleosome remodelling activity comparable to the wild-type protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by activity assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pairs of cysteine residues were introduced at specific sites in Chd1 1–1305 for PELDOR measurements.
source: Pairs of cysteine residues were then introduced at specific sites in Chd1 1–1305 via site-directed mutagenesis and these sites were then labelled with the thiol-reactive reporter (1-Oxyl-2,2,5,5-tetramethylpyrroline-3-methyl) methanethiosulfonate (MTSL).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for PELDOR measurements.

claim: The experimentally measured distances from PELDOR correlate with the predicted distances derived from the chromoATPase crystal structure to within a few angstroms.
source: The experimentally measured distances correlate with the predicted distances derived from the chromoATPase crystal structure (3MWY) (Hauk et al., 2010) to within a few angstroms (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental PELDOR data with predictions from a crystal structure.

claim: The structure of the chromoATPase domains is similar in solution to that observed in the crystal structure.
source: This suggests that the structure of the chromoATPase domains is similar in solution to that observed in the crystal structure.
evidence: This is an inference from the agreement between PELDOR measurements and crystal structure predictions.

claim: A total of 16 distinct distance measurements were made between different pairwise combinations of sites in the DBD and chromoATPase domains.
source: A total of 16 distinct distance measurements were made between different pairwise combinations of these sites.
evidence: This describes the extent of PELDOR measurements performed.

claim: Measurements between locations within the DBD and ATPase lobe 1 gave rise to several well defined measurements.
source: Measurements between locations within the DBD and ATPase lobe 1 gave rise to several well defined measurements where an oscillation is evident in the background corrected signal and a single major distance distribution can be extracted (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This describes the quality of PELDOR data for specific domain pairs.

claim: Measurements between ATPase lobe 2 and the DBD were less well defined, often giving rise to multiple distance distributions.
source: However, measurements between ATPase lobe 2 and the DBD were in general less well defined, often giving rise to multiple distance distributions with similar probabilities (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes the quality of PELDOR data for specific domain pairs.

claim: The less well defined measurements between ATPase lobe 2 and the DBD likely arise from increased dynamics between these domains.
source: This is likely to arise from increased dynamics between these domains.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the PELDOR data quality.

claim: Measurements between chromodomains and the DBD did not provide tight single distance distributions.
source: Similarly, measurements between chromodomains and the DBD did not provide tight single distance distributions (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This describes the quality of PELDOR data for specific domain pairs.

claim: Two separate modelling approaches were used to determine the orientation of the DBD relative to the chromoATPase domains using PELDOR distance constraints.
source: The most prominent distribution of distances for each pair of labelling sites (Shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 3–5) was used as a constraint in two separate modelling approaches.
evidence: This describes the computational modeling approach.

claim: Xplor-NIH was used for conjugated gradient minimisation with PELDOR distance constraints.
source: In the first approach, a conjugated gradient minimisation was carried with centres of the modelled distribution of the nitroxide atoms NOE constraints in Xplor-NIH (Schwieters et al., 2003) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes one computational modeling approach used.

claim: TagDock was used to compute geometrically possible docking poses between the domains and evaluate those compatible with experimental distance constraints.
source: In the second, TagDock (Smith et al., 2013) was used to compute all geometrically possible docking poses between the domains and evaluated those compatible with experimental distance constraints.
evidence: This describes the second computational modeling approach used.

claim: The Xplor approach yielded an ensemble of solutions with RMSD 2.8 Å.
source: In both Xplor and TagDock approaches, an ensemble of solutions with RMSD 2.8 and 1.6 Å, respectively, were obtained.
evidence: This is a result from the computational modeling.

claim: The TagDock approach yielded an ensemble of solutions with RMSD 1.6 Å.
source: In both Xplor and TagDock approaches, an ensemble of solutions with RMSD 2.8 and 1.6 Å, respectively, were obtained.
evidence: This is a result from the computational modeling.

claim: The average of the ensemble solutions obtained using the two approaches has an RMS deviation of 2.4 Å.
source: In addition, the average of the ensemble solutions obtained using the two approaches has an RMS deviation of 2.4 Å.
evidence: This is a comparison of the two modeling approaches.

claim: The PELDOR-derived model is compatible with the volume envelopes obtained from the SAXS data.
source: The PELDOR-derived model is compatible with the volume envelopes obtained from the SAXS data (Figure 2—figure supplement 7A).
evidence: This is a comparison of PELDOR and SAXS data.

claim: The SAXS pattern computed from the atomistic EPR-based model of Chd1 yields a poor fit to the experimental scattering data from the full length protein with discrepancy χ2= 11.5.
source: The SAXS pattern computed by program CRYSOL (Svergun et al., 1995) from the atomistic EPR-based model of Chd1 yields a poor fit to the experimental scattering data from the full length protein with discrepancy χ2= 11.5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of model and experimental data.

claim: Significant parts of the Chd1 polypeptide are missing in the EPR-based model, which explains the poor fit to SAXS data.
source: However, this misfit is to be expected given that significant parts of the polypeptide (174 and 36 residues at the N- and C-termini, respectively, and a 82-residue linker between chromoATPase and DBD domains) are missing in the Chd1 model.
evidence: This is an explanation for the discrepancy between model and data.

claim: The program BUNCH was used to reconstruct probable configurations of missing portions of Chd1 as dummy residue chains.
source: To address this, the program BUNCH was used to reconstruct probable configurations of these missing portions in the form of dummy residue (DR) chains (Petoukhov and Svergun, 2005).
evidence: This describes a computational approach to improve the model.

claim: The addition of the missing loops significantly improved the agreement between the experimental and the calculated SAXS data with χ2 improving from 11.5 to 2.08.
source: The addition of the missing loops significantly improved the agreement between the experimental and the calculated data with χ2 improving from 11.5 to 2.08 (Figure 2—figure supplement 7B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing improved model fit.

claim: Chemical crosslinking coupled with mass spectrometry using BS3 identified several crosslinks between the N-terminal region of Chd1 and the DBD.
source: Interestingly, several crosslinks between the N-terminal region of Chd1 and the DBD are also identified (Figure 3A), suggesting these two regions are close to one another in the intact protein.
evidence: This is a result from crosslinking mass spectrometry experiments.

claim: The N-terminal region of Chd1 and the DBD are close to one another in the intact protein.
source: Interestingly, several crosslinks between the N-terminal region of Chd1 and the DBD are also identified (Figure 3A), suggesting these two regions are close to one another in the intact protein.
evidence: This is an inference from crosslinking data.

claim: The isolated recombinant DBD is able to form an intermolecular complex with a truncated form of Chd1 (residues 1–1010) lacking the DBD.
source: We observe that the isolated recombinant DBD is still able to form an intermolecular complex with a truncated form of Chd1 (residues 1–1010) lacking the DBD (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from gel-filtration experiments.

claim: When the N-terminal 133 amino acids are removed from Chd1, the complex with the DBD is no longer formed.
source: Furthermore, when the N-terminal 133 amino acids are removed from Chd1 this complex with the DBD is no longer formed (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from gel-filtration experiments with a deletion mutant.

claim: Contacts between the N-terminus of Chd1 directly contribute to the association with the DBD.
source: This suggests that contacts between the N-terminus of Chd1 directly contribute to the association with the DBD.
evidence: This is an inference from the gel-filtration data with deletion mutants.

claim: There is considerable conservation within the 133 amino acids N-terminal to the chromodomains across different yeast species.
source: There is considerable conservation within the 133 amino acids N-terminal to the chromodomains and this includes a tract of acidic amino acids (57-88) followed by a positively charged region extending from 90 to 120.
evidence: This is an observation from sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The N-terminal region of Chd1 includes a tract of acidic amino acids (57-88) followed by a positively charged region extending from 90 to 120.
source: There is considerable conservation within the 133 amino acids N-terminal to the chromodomains and this includes a tract of acidic amino acids (57-88) followed by a positively charged region extending from 90 to 120.
evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis.

claim: Deletion of residues 57–88 results in loss of interaction with the DBD.
source: Indeed, when we delete just residues 57–88 the interaction with the DBD is also lost (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a result from gel-filtration experiments with a deletion mutant.

claim: The acidic patch (residues 57-88) plays an important role in mediating interactions with the DBD.
source: Thus, this acidic patch appears to play an important role in mediating interactions with the DBD.
evidence: This is an inference from the deletion mutant data.

claim: Deletion of the acidic patch (△57–88) increased nucleosome sliding activity 2-fold.
source: Deletion of the acidic patch was observed to increase nucleosome sliding 2-fold, while deletion of the basic region shows no sliding activity (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome repositioning assays.

claim: Deletion of the basic region (△90-120) shows no sliding activity.
source: Deletion of the acidic patch was observed to increase nucleosome sliding 2-fold, while deletion of the basic region shows no sliding activity (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome repositioning assays.

claim: Deletion of the entire N-terminal 133 amino acids increased activity 1.5-fold.
source: Deletion of the entire N-terminal 133 amino acids increased activity 1.5-fold (data not shown), while deletion of the extreme N-terminal 35 residues reduced activity 20-fold (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome repositioning assays.

claim: Deletion of the extreme N-terminal 35 residues reduced activity 20-fold.
source: Deletion of the entire N-terminal 133 amino acids increased activity 1.5-fold (data not shown), while deletion of the extreme N-terminal 35 residues reduced activity 20-fold (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome repositioning assays.

claim: Triple mutation of three conserved lysine residues within the basic region resulted in a greater than 10-fold reduction in activity.
source: Triple mutation of three conserved lysine residues within the basic region resulted in a greater than 10-fold reduction in activity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome repositioning assays.

claim: N-terminal mutants affected ATPase activity, with reduced or increased activity generally correlating with nucleosome sliding activity.
source: These mutants also affected ATPase activity, with reduced or increased activity generally correlating with nucleosome sliding activity (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a result from ATP hydrolysis assays.

claim: The increased activity of Chd1 △ 57–88 arose primarily from an increased Kcat.
source: The increased activity of Chd1 △ 57–88 arose primarily from an increased Kcat (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a result from kinetic analysis of ATP hydrolysis.

claim: Chd1 △ 57–88 formed complexes with nucleosomes in the apo state more effectively than wild-type as detected in gel shift assays.
source: In addition, this mutant formed complexes with nucleosomes in the apo state more effectively as detected in gel shift assays (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome binding assays.

claim: The Chd1 △ 90–120, △ 1–35 and R20-21A mutations that strongly reduced activity also bound nucleosomes weakly.
source: The Chd1 △ 90–120, △ 1–35 and R20-21A mutations that strongly reduced activity also bound nucleosomes weakly (Figure 4D), while deletion of residues 1–35 enhanced nucleosome binding but was deleterious to enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is a result from nucleosome binding assays.

claim: A more flexible linkage between the ATPase and DBD facilitates productive engagement with nucleosomes.
source: As both the Chd1 △ 57–88 and △ 1–133 deletions that increase activity reduce association between the ATPase and DBD (Figure 3), we speculate that a more flexible linkage facilitates productive engagement with nucleosomes while inactivating mutations may orient these domains less favourably for full activity.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the correlation between activity and domain interactions.

claim: Full length Chd1 or Chd1 △ 57–88 were integrated into the CHD1 locus of an isw1△chd1△ mutant strain for in vivo analysis.
source: To investigate the consequences of this change in activity in vivo, full length Chd1 or Chd1 △ 57–88 were integrated into the CHD1 locus of an isw1△chd1△ mutant strain.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for in vivo studies.

claim: In an isw1△chd1△ mutant strain, positioning of coding region nucleosomes is severely compromised and is partially restored when full length CHD1 is reintegrated.
source: In this strain, positioning of coding region nucleosomes is severely compromised and is partially restored when full length CHD1 is reintegrated (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a result from MNase-Seq analysis.

claim: When chd1 △ 57–88 is reintegrated, a nucleosomal oscillation is restored with slightly greater amplitude than the wild type.
source: When chd1 △ 57–88 is reintegrated, a nucleosomal oscillation is restored with slightly greater amplitude than the wild type.
evidence: This is a result from MNase-Seq analysis.

claim: The maximal density of nucleosome dyads is offset downstream by four base pairs at nucleosome +3 in the chd1 △ 57–88 strain.
source: In addition, the maximal density of nucleosome dyads is offset downstream by four base pairs at nucleosome +3 and increments of approximately four base pairs at subsequent downstream nucleosomes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from MNase-Seq analysis.

claim: The offset in nucleosome positioning in chd1 △ 57–88 is consistent with increased spacing between coding region nucleosomes with alignment to the transcriptional start site retained.
source: This is consistent with increased spacing between coding region nucleosomes with alignment to the transcriptional start site (TSS) retained.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the MNase-Seq data.

claim: Introduction of full length Chd1 on a higher copy number plasmid resulted in a > 3-fold increase in expression.
source: To test whether the total amount of Chd1 activity affected inter-nucleosome spacing full length Chd1 was introduced on a higher copy number plasmid, resulting in a > 3 – fold increase in expression as assessed by Western blotting (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from Western blotting.

claim: Overexpression of full length Chd1 caused a slightly greater increase in nucleosome spacing, approximately six base pairs.
source: The alignment of nucleosomal reads to the genome from this strain indicates a slightly greater increase in nucleosome spacing, approximately six base pairs (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a result from MNase-Seq analysis.

claim: Introduction of chd1 △ 57–88 on the high copy pRS423 plasmid caused a further increase in spacing to approximately 26 base pairs.
source: Introduction of chd1 △ 57–88 on the high copy pRS423 plasmid caused a further increase in spacing to approximately 26 base pairs (Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 3).
evidence: This is a result from MNase-Seq analysis.

claim: Coding region internucleosome spacing is influenced by the level of Chd1 activity present.
source: These observations are consistent with coding region internucleosome spacing being influenced by the level of Chd1 activity present.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vivo nucleosome spacing data.

claim: Chd1 can establish arrays of nucleosomes with a range of linker lengths in vivo.
source: They also show that Chd1 can establish arrays of nucleosomes with a range of linker lengths in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vivo nucleosome spacing data.

claim: Variable nucleosome spacing may result from competition between different enzymes involved in establishing nucleosome phasing in vivo.
source: It may result from competition between different enzymes involved in establishing nucleosome phasing in vivo (Ocampo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of variable nucleosome spacing.

claim: Variable nucleosome spacing may result from changes in nucleosome density following alteration of Chd1 activity in chromatin assembly.
source: From changes in nucleosome density following alteration of Chd1 activity in chromatin assembly (Lusser et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of variable nucleosome spacing.

claim: Variable nucleosome spacing may result because increased nucleosome phasing activity drives nucleosomes apart via a statistically driven process.
source: Or simply because increased nucleosome phasing activity drives nucleosomes apart via a statistically driven process (Mavrich et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of variable nucleosome spacing.

claim: Complexes between Chd1 1–1305 and nucleosomes with symmetrical 25 bp linkers were studied by cryo-EM in the apo state.
source: We next sought to study the interaction of Chd1 when engaged with nucleosomes. Cryo-EM was adopted to achieve this and we initially studied the interaction of Chd1 1–1305 with nucleosomes with symmetrical 25 bp linkers using this approach.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for cryo-EM studies.

claim: A volume was obtained for the Chd1-nucleosome apo complex with a resolution of approximately 20 Å.
source: Following 3D classification and refinement, a volume was obtained with a resolution of approximately 20 Å (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is a result from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The in solution model for Chd1 and a mononucleosome could be fitted into the cryo-EM volume of the apo complex.
source: This volume is made up of separate areas into which our in solution model for Chd1 and a mononucleosome could be fitted (Figure 6E).
evidence: This describes the fitting of models into the cryo-EM volume.

claim: The engagement surface between Chd1 and the mononucleosome in the apo state is minimal.
source: A notable feature of this fit is that the engagement surface between Chd1 and the mononucleosome is minimal.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: In the apo state, Chd1 is bound through interactions between the DBD and the ATPase domains are not engaged.
source: The simplest explanation for this mode of engagement would be that Chd1 is bound through interactions between the DBD and the ATPase domains are not engaged.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Hyperactive mutants of Chd1, △ 57–88 and △ 1–133, formed complexes with nucleosomes that migrated slightly faster on native gels.
source: We noticed that the hyperactive mutants of Chd1, △ 57–88 and△ 1–133, formed complexes with nucleosomes that migrated slightly faster on native gels (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an observation from native gel electrophoresis.

claim: The faster migration of hyperactive mutant-nucleosome complexes on native gels suggests a more compact structure.
source: This suggests a more compact structure.
evidence: This is an inference from the gel mobility data.

claim: Complexes between Chd1 △ 57–88 and nucleosomes bearing an 11 bp asymmetric linker were assembled in the presence of ADP-BeFx for cryo-EM analysis.
source: To characterise this further, complexes between Chd1 △ 57–88 and nucleosomes bearing an 11 bp asymmetric linker were assembled. This linker was selected to reduce the number of different conformations via which Chd1 could potentially interact via it's DBD. These complexes were formed in the presence of the non-hydrolysable ATP analogue ADP-BeFx which has been observed to stimulate binding of other enzymes to nucleosomes (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Racki et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for cryo-EM studies of the engaged complex.

claim: 2450 movies were collected for the Chd1 △ 57–88-nucleosome complex and from these 280,000 particles were picked.
source: 2450 movies were collected and from these 280,000 particles picked.
evidence: This describes the data collection for cryo-EM.

claim: 197,602 particles could be assigned into 2D classes consistent with a nucleosome with a bound attachment.
source: 197,602 of these could be assigned into 2D classes that were consistent with a nucleosome with a bound attachment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the image processing for cryo-EM.

claim: The final volume for the Chd1 △ 57–88-nucleosome complex has a resolution of 15 Å.
source: Solvent masking was applied prior to the final refinement which resulted in a final volume with a resolution of 15 Å (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: A nucleosome can be docked within the cryo-EM volume of the engaged complex.
source: A nucleosome can be docked within the volume and the DNA volume on the side of the nucleosome lacking linker provides a strong reference point to orient the nucleosome (Figure 7; Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the fitting of structures into the cryo-EM volume.

claim: The position of the chromoATPase is unambiguous in the cryo-EM volume of the engaged complex.
source: The position of the chromoATPase is also unambiguous and the protrusion formed by ATPase lobe 2 and the chromodomains allows the domains to be oriented (Figure 7; Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the fitting of structures into the cryo-EM volume.

claim: Solvent masking was required to reveal the trajectory of the linker DNA in the cryo-EM volume.
source: While the volume occupied by the DBD must be in the general vicinity of the 11 bp linker, solvent masking was required to reveal the trajectory of the linker DNA.
evidence: This describes the image processing approach.

claim: There is a major change in the orientation of the DBD with respect to ATPase lobe 1 between the solution structure and the nucleosome engaged structure.
source: When the alignment of Chd1 DBD and ATPase domain is compared between the solution structure determined by PELDOR and SAXS (Figures 1 and 2) to that in the nucleosome engaged structure (Figure 7), it is clear that a major change in the orientation of the DBD with respect to ATPase lobe 1 takes place (Figure 7—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a comparison of structural models.

claim: Docking Chd1 in the solution conformation onto a nucleosome using the location of the chromoATPase domains in the engaged state as a reference point results in steric clashes with the histone octamer.
source: If Chd1 in the conformation observed in solution is docked onto a nucleosome using the location of the chromoATPase domains in the engaged state as a reference point, steric clashes with the histone octamer indicate this is not possible (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a result from structural modeling.

claim: The nucleosomal DNA adjacent to the linker is unravelled from the octamer surface in the engaged complex.
source: A prominent feature of the structural model is that the nucleosomal DNA adjacent to the linker is unravelled from the octamer surface.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: When intact nucleosomal DNA is modelled into the cryo-EM volume it protrudes into a region of missing density.
source: This is evident as when intact nucleosomal DNA is modelled into the volume it protrudes into a region of missing density (Figure 7—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an observation from modeling into the cryo-EM volume.

claim: Fluorescent dyes were introduced to DNA derived from the 601 nucleosome positioning sequence at specific positions for FRET measurements.
source: Fluorescent dyes were introduced to DNA derived from the 601 nucleosome positioning sequence on either the forward (F) or reverse (R) strand at the indicated positions relative to the nucleosomal dyad axis of symmetry (Figure 8A; Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach for FRET measurements.

claim: When Chd1 1–1305 was added to nucleosomes labeled at F−71 and F + 14, no change in FRET efficiency was observed.
source: When Chd1 1–1305 was added to these nucleosomes, no change in FRET efficiency was observed (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: The lack of FRET change at F−71 and F + 14 is consistent with the six base pair linker being too short to direct binding of the Chd1 DBD on this side of the nucleosome.
source: This is consistent with the six base pair linker being too short to direct binding of the Chd1 DBD on this side of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRET data.

claim: Binding of Chd1 1–1305 in presence of AMP-PNP caused a reduction in the mean FRET efficiency from 0.5 to 0.3 for nucleosomes labeled at F + 2 and R-66.
source: In contrast, when nucleosomal DNA was labelled at F + 2 with Tamra and at R-66 with Alexa647, binding of Chd1 1–1305 in presence of AMP-PNP caused a reduction in the mean FRET efficiency from 0.5 to 0.3 (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: The FRET change at F + 2 and R-66 is consistent with Chd1 binding causing DNA nine base pairs from the edge of the nucleosome to dissociate.
source: This is consistent with Chd1 binding causing DNA nine base pairs from the edge of the nucleosome to dissociate in a fashion similar to that observed with Chd1 △57–88 by single particle cryo EM (Figure 7; Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRET data in the context of the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Chd1 △57–88 causes a similar change in FRET efficiency between F + 2 and R-66 to that observed for Chd1 1–1305, both in the presence of AMP-PNP and ADP-BeFx.
source: Indeed, Chd1 △57–88 causes a similar change in FRET efficiency between F + 2 Tamara and R-66 Alexa 647 to that observed for Chd1 1–1305, both in the presence of AMP-PNP (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A), and ADP-BeFx (Figure 8—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: The dissociation of nucleosomal DNA did not extend deep in the nucleosome as a reporter site at R-60 was unaffected by Chd1 binding.
source: The dissociation of nucleosomal DNA did not extend deep in the nucleosome as a reporter site at R-60 was unaffected by Chd1 binding (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: A site at R-85 showed a larger change in FRET efficiency from 0.45 to 0.1 upon binding of Chd1.
source: A site further into the linker, namely R-85 showed a larger change in FRET efficiency from 0.45 to 0.1 upon binding of Chd1 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: The reduction in FRET efficiency at R-85 was more prominent in the presence of Chd1 1–1305 and AMP-PNP than in the presence of Chd1 1–1305 alone.
source: This made it possible to show that the reduction in FRET efficiency was more prominent in the presence of Chd1 1–1305 and AMP-PNP than it was in the presence of Chd1 1–1305 alone (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a result from FRET measurements.

claim: In the presence of AMP-PNP, the unwrapped state was favored both as a result of an increased rate of transition to the unwrapped state and a reduction to the rate of DNA re-association.
source: In the presence of AMP-PNP, the unwrapped state was favored both as a result of an increased rate of transition to the unwrapped state and a reduction to the rate of DNA re-association (Figure 8—figure supplement 3F).
evidence: This is a result from kinetic analysis of FRET data.

claim: DNA unwrapping occurs with a non-mutant form of Chd1 similar to that observed with Chd1 △57–88 by single particle EM.
source: These observations indicate that DNA unwrapping occurs with a non-mutant form of Chd1 similar to that observed with Chd1 △57–88 by single particle EM (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRET data in the context of the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Unwrapping is favoured in a nucleotide-bound state consistent with the distinct configurations of Chd1 observed in the absence and presence of ADP-BeFx.
source: In addition, unwrapping is favoured in a nucleotide-bound state consistent with the distinct configurations of Chd1 observed in the absence (Figure 6) and presence of ADP- BeFx (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRET data in the context of the cryo-EM structures.

claim: The dissociation of the outer turn of DNA during the formation of the engaged complex may serve to prime the nucleosome for dynamics driven by ATP-hydrolysis.
source: The dissociation of the outer turn of DNA during the formation of this engaged complex may serve to prime the nucleosome for dynamics driven by ATP-hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of DNA unwrapping.

claim: Chd1 can engage with the nucleosome in different modes.
source: We observe that Chd1 can engage with the nucleosome in different modes (Figures 6 and 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the structural findings.

claim: Chd1 can interact with nucleosomes in additional conformations beyond those characterized in this study.
source: It is likely that Chd1 can interact with nucleosomes in additional conformations as this study is not exhaustive in characterising a full spectrum of complexes that can be formed with different linker DNA lengths and in different stages of ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a speculation about the limitations of the study.

claim: Complexes with two molecules of Chd1 bound to one nucleosome can be formed but have not been characterised in this study.
source: In addition, complexes with two molecules of Chd1 bound to one nucleosome can be formed but have not been characterised here.
evidence: This is a statement about the scope of the study.

claim: Ensemble approaches that have previously been used to characterise the interaction of Chd1 and other remodelling enzymes with nucleosomes may report on a mixture of different states.
source: Because Chd1 can engage with nucleosomes in different ways, it is possible that ensemble approaches that have previously been used to characterise the interaction of Chd1 and other remodelling enzymes with nucleosomes may report on a mixture of different states.
evidence: This is a speculation about the interpretation of previous studies.

claim: The SANT-SLIDE domains of Chd1 and the related domains in ISWI bind DNA with affinities in the low nanomolar range.
source: The SANT-SLIDE domains of Chd1 and the related domains in ISWI, bind DNA with affinities in the low nanomolar range and are required for efficient interaction with nucleosomes (Grüne et al., 2003; Ryan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: DNA recognition by Chd1 does not appear to be sequence specific.
source: DNA recognition by Chd1 does not appear to be sequence specific (Sharma et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The related DBD of Isw1a has been observed to interact with different regions of linker DNA dependent on the nucleosomal substrate used.
source: Consistent with this, the related DBD of Isw1a has been observed to interact with different regions of linker DNA dependent on the nucleosomal substrate used (Yamada et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Interaction of the DBD with linker DNA may represent a first step in the association of Chd1 with chromatin.
source: It is possible that interaction of the DBD with linker DNA represents a first step in the association of Chd1 with chromatin.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of Chd1 binding to chromatin.

claim: One-dimensional diffusive motion provides a means for enrichment on longer linker DNA and a means of scanning exposed linker DNA.
source: One-dimensional diffusive motion that has been observed for many non-specific DNA-binding proteins (Stanford et al., 2000) provides a means for enrichment on longer linker DNA and a means of scanning exposed linker DNA for sites where engagement of the ATPase domains with nucleosomes is also possible.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of Chd1 binding to chromatin, supported by a citation about DNA-binding proteins.

claim: The DBD is bound close to the edge of the nucleosome interacting with the first 10 base pairs of linker DNA in the engaged complex.
source: The DBD is bound close to the edge of the nucleosome interacting with the first 10 base pairs of linker DNA.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Chd1 activity is greatly reduced when the SANT and SLIDE domains that comprise the C-terminal DBD are deleted.
source: Previous studies have shown that Chd1 activity is greatly reduced when the SANT and SLIDE domains that comprise the C-terminal DBD are deleted (Hauk et al., 2010; Ryan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Fusion of Chd1 to heterologous domains that direct specific interactions with DNA restores activity.
source: Remarkably, fusion of Chd1 to heterologous domains that direct specific interactions with DNA restores activity (McKnight et al., 2011; Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Chd1-AraC hybrids are dependent on an araI site and the optimal position for this is +8 bp from the nucleosome boundary.
source: Chd1-AraC hybrids are dependent on an araI site and the optimal position for this is +8 bp from the nucleosome boundary (McKnight et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Chd1-streptavidin fusions are dependent on the introduction of biotinylated nucleotides with optimal location +11 bp from the nucleosome boundary.
source: Chd1-streptavidin fusions are dependent on the introduction of biotinylated nucleotides with optimal location +11 bp from the nucleosome boundary (Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: An interaction with the first turn of DNA outside of the nucleosome, as observed in the engaged structure, is functionally important.
source: Although these fusion proteins will not pack identically to the native SANT and SLIDE domains, these observations indicate that an interaction with the first turn of DNA outside of the nucleosome, as observed in our engaged structure, is functionally important.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM structure in the context of previous functional studies.

claim: Nucleosome repositioning is directed towards the bound linker.
source: They also show that nucleosome repositioning is directed towards the bound linker (McKnight et al., 2011; Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The loss of octamer contacts on the bound side of the nucleosome will reduce the energy required to affect dynamic alterations to nucleosomal DNA.
source: The loss of octamer contacts on the bound side of the nucleosome will reduce the energy required to affect dynamic alterations to nucleosomal DNA and may act as a priming step for subsequent ATP-dependent remodelling.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of DNA unwrapping.

claim: DNA unwrapping may act as a priming step for subsequent ATP-dependent remodelling.
source: The loss of octamer contacts on the bound side of the nucleosome will reduce the energy required to affect dynamic alterations to nucleosomal DNA and may act as a priming step for subsequent ATP-dependent remodelling.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of DNA unwrapping.

claim: This priming step may distinguish the initial ATP dependent changes from subsequent cycles of activity.
source: This priming step may distinguish the initial ATP dependent changes from subsequent cycles of activity.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of remodeling.

claim: Seven base pairs of DNA have been observed to be removed from nucleosomes following the action of ISW2 and Isw1b complexes followed by subsequent three base pair movements.
source: Consistent with this seven base pairs of DNA have been observed to be removed from nucleosomes following the action of ISW2 and Isw1b complexes followed by subsequent three base pair movements (Deindl et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: ATP-dependent repositioning occurs as a result of the action of the chromoATPase domain which engages with nucleosomal DNA, centred 1.5 superhelical turns off the nucleosomal dyad.
source: ATP-dependent repositioning occurs as a result of the action of the chromoATPase domain which engages with nucleosomal DNA, centred 1.5 superhelical turns off the nucleosomal dyad (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The SHL 1.5 location that is bound by Chd1 is further away on the linear DNA sequence, separated by 90 rather than 60 base pairs from the bound linker.
source: The SHL 1.5 location that is bound is further away on the linear DNA sequence, separated by 90 rather than 60 base pairs from the bound linker.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The SHL 1.5 location bound by Chd1 is in closer spatial proximity to the bound linker once DNA has been wrapped around the nucleosome.
source: However, it is in closer spatial proximity once DNA has been wrapped around the nucleosome (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The arrangement of Chd1 on nucleosomes is different to that previously reported for ISW2.
source: This arrangement is different to that previously reported for ISW2.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous studies.

claim: In ISW2, the proximal dyad location in the DNA sequence is bound by the ATPase domains.
source: In this case, the proximal dyad location in the DNA sequence is bound by the ATPase domains (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The distinct topography with which the domains of Chd1 engage with nucleosomal DNA raise the possibility that the orientation of DNA translocation is also different to that observed with other enzymes.
source: The distinct topography with which the domains of Chd1 engage with nucleosomal DNA raise the possibility that the orientation of DNA translocation is also different to that observed with other enzymes (Saha et al., 2005; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of DNA translocation.

claim: The resolution of the cryo-EM structure does not enable assignment of the strand specificity of nucleic acid contacts.
source: High-resolution structures enable the strand specificity of nucleic acid contacts to be assigned (Sengoku et al., 2006). However, our structure is not at a resolution where this assignment can be made, so the directionality of translocation cannot be resolved.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the structural data.

claim: The limited resolution does not enable comment on rearrangements anticipated to occur between the chromo and ATPase domains and within the ATPase domains during engagement with DNA.
source: Similarly, the limited resolution does not enable us to comment on rearrangements that are anticipated to occur between the chromo and ATPase domains and within the ATPase domains during engagement with DNA (Hauk and Bowman, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the structural data.

claim: A recent study identifies cross-links between Chd1 and nucleosomal DNA.
source: A recent study identifies cross-links between Chd1 and nucleosomal DNA (Nodelman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a reference to a recent study.

claim: The major DNA contacts made by the DBD, chromo domains and ATPase domain identified by crosslinking are consistent with the model presented in Figure 7.
source: The major DNA contacts made by the DBD, chromo domains and ATPase domain are consistent with the model presented in Figure 7.
evidence: This is a comparison with a recent crosslinking study.

claim: The cryo-EM model is reinforced by orthologous single-molecule FRET and cross-linking data.
source: As a result our model derived from cryo-EM is reinforced by orthologous single-molecule FRET and cross-linking building understanding of how a near intact remodeling enzyme interacts with a nucleosome.
evidence: This is a summary of the complementary evidence supporting the model.

claim: A large-scale nucleotide-dependent change in conformation of the related enzyme SNF2h has been reported previously.
source: A large-scale nucleotide-dependent change in conformation of the related enzyme SNF2h has been reported previously (Leonard and Narlikar, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The SNF2h conformational change involves repositioning of the SNF2h SANT-SLIDE DBD from a site that generates a FRET signal with a site +20 bp from the nucleosome edge to one that generates FRET at a site at −25 internal to a nucleosome.
source: This involves repositioning of the SNF2h SANT-SLIDE DBD from a site that generates a FRET signal with a site +20 bp from the nucleosome edge to one that generates FRET at a site at −25 internal to a nucleosome.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The SNF2h conformational change could involve redistribution of the SNF2h SANT SLIDE domain from positions distributed along the linker to high occupancy at the nucleosome boundary.
source: It is possible that this could involve redistribution of the SNF2h SANT SLIDE domain from positions distributed along the linker to high occupancy at the nucleosome boundary.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of the SNF2h conformational change.

claim: Evidence for a conformational change upon binding to DNA and nucleosomes has been obtained by studying changes in protease digestion of Drosophila ISWI following binding to DNA.
source: Additional evidence for a conformational change upon binding to DNA and nucleosomes has been obtained by studying changes in protease digestion of Drosophila ISWI following binding to DNA (Mueller-Planitz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The predominant conformation observed in solution is not capable of binding nucleosomes in the fully engaged conformation which is assumed to be active.
source: Nonetheless, the major species observed in solution is not capable of binding nucleosomes in the fully engaged conformation which we assume to be active.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: The apo protein could be considered to be auto inhibited.
source: As a result, the apo protein could be considered to be auto inhibited.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: Mutations have been reported that increase activity within Chd1 and other remodelling ATPases.
source: Consistent with this, both within Chd1 (Figure 4; [Hauk et al., 2010]) and other remodelling ATPases (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Liu et al., 2015), mutations have been reported that increase activity.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and data in this manuscript.

claim: Mutations to the N terminus that increase activity reduce interactions between the DBD and the chromoATPase.
source: Here, we show that mutations to the N terminus that increase activity, reduce interactions between the DBD and the chromoATPase (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a result from the study.

claim: Increased flexibility in the orientation of the chromoATPase and DBD increases the opportunity for productive engagement with nucleosomes.
source: This suggests that increased flexibility in the orientation of the chromoATPase and DBD increases the opportunity for productive engagement with nucleosomes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mutagenesis data.

claim: Regulation of accessory domain orientation to enable engagement with the nucleosomal substrate represents a potent means of regulating the activity of remodelling ATPases.
source: As a result, regulation of accessory domain orientation to enable engagement with the nucleosomal substrate represents a potent means of regulating the activity of remodelling ATPases.
evidence: This is a general conclusion about the regulation of remodeling enzymes.

claim: The combined abundance of chromatin remodelling enzymes could present a load on nuclear ATP levels.
source: This may be important as the combined abundance of chromatin remodelling enzymes (Flaus and Owen-Hughes, 2011) could present a load on nuclear ATP levels.
evidence: This is a speculation about the physiological importance of regulation.

claim: Regulation allowing increased activity when chromatin organisation is required would reduce the energy expended organising chromatin.
source: Regulation allowing increased activity when chromatin organisation is required, for example following transcription or DNA replication would reduce the energy expended organising chromatin.
evidence: This is a speculation about the physiological importance of regulation.

claim: Chd1 plays a major role in the maintenance of even nucleosome spacing within coding regions.
source: Chd1 plays a major role in the maintenance of even nucleosome spacing within coding regions (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The activity of Chd1 is anticipated to be influenced by the length of DNA between adjacent nucleosomes.
source: To achieve this, the activity of the enzyme is also anticipated to be influenced by the length of DNA between adjacent nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of nucleosome spacing.

claim: Within the ISWI related ACF complex, the duration of pauses prior to repositioning is shortened when linker lengths are increased in the range 40 to 60 bp.
source: Within the ISWI related ACF complex, the duration of pauses prior to repositioning is shortened when linker lengths are increased in the range 40 to 60 bp (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: An activation mutation termed AutoN, N-terminal to the ATPase domains, is found to impede DNA length sensing in ACF.
source: An activation mutation termed AutoN (Clapier and Cairns, 2012), N-terminal to the ATPase domains, is found to impede DNA length sensing (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The AutoN mutation may function in a similar way to the hyperactive Chd1 △ 57–88 mutant, enabling engagement with nucleosomes in an active conformation independent of linker DNA length.
source: This may function in a similar way to the hyperactive Chd1 △ 57–88 mutant, enabling engagement with nucleosomes in an active conformation independent of linker DNA length.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of the AutoN mutation.

claim: There may be important differences in the way in which the SANT-SLIDE domains of ISWI and Chd1 related proteins act.
source: However, there may also be important differences in the way in which the SANT-SLIDE domains of ISWI and Chd1 related proteins act.
evidence: This is a speculation about differences between enzymes.

claim: The structures of the SANT-SLIDE domains differ significantly in ISWI and Chd1.
source: The structures of these domains do differ significantly in ISWI and Chd1 (Grüne et al., 2003; Ryan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Yeast Chd1 acts to organise nucleosomes with relatively short linker lengths of 16 base pairs within yeast coding regions.
source: In addition, yeast Chd1 acts to organise nucleosomes with relatively short linker lengths of 16 base pairs within yeast coding regions (Gkikopoulos et al., 2011; Ocampo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Engagement with the first turn of extranucleosomal DNA provides a means of achieving activity within close packed nucleosome arrays.
source: In this respect, engagement with the first turn of extranucleosomal DNA as we observe (Figure 7) provides a means of achieving activity within close packed nucleosome arrays.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data in the context of in vivo function.

claim: Steric clashes with the SANT-SLIDE-bound linker would be anticipated to get progressively more serious when the linker between nucleosomes is reduced below 20 bp with the effect of reducing enzyme activity.
source: Nonetheless, steric clashes with the SANT-SLIDE-bound linker would be anticipated to get progressively more serious when the linker between nucleosomes is reduced below 20 bp with the effect of reducing enzyme activity.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of linker length sensing.

claim: The inhibition of repositioning when linker length falls below a low limit is sufficient to drive the even spacing of nucleosomes via a bidirectional statistically driven process.
source: The inhibition of repositioning when linker length falls below a low limit is sufficient to drive the even spacing of nucleosomes via a bidirectional statistically driven process (Blosser et al., 2009; Mavrich et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of nucleosome spacing, supported by citations.
